patch.value: Semicolon-free class fields bypass docstring evaluation

Found by Greptile on PR 33 and confirmed by reading skipMemberRest. The helper consumes tokens until a semicolon, a closing brace or end of file, so in an exported class written without semicolons every field after the first is consumed as part of the first field's trailing type or initialiser and never judged. The repository's own style uses semicolons everywhere, which is why the suite did not catch it, but a gate that depends on the code under test using one particular optional token is not fail-closed. A fix needs an automatic-semicolon-insertion heuristic narrow enough to avoid splitting a multi-line initialiser: stop when the next token begins a new line, the previous token could end an expression, and the next token could begin a member.

An exported class with semicolon-free fields has every public member judged; a field with a multi-line initialiser or a multi-line conditional is not split; no false positive appears on the repository's own sources
